title: Saudi Arabia Joins BRICS
reason: The year and country hold — on 24 August 2023, at the BRICS summit in Johannesburg, South African President Ramaphosa announced Saudi Arabia was one of six countries (alongside Argentina, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the UAE) invited to join BRICS effective 1 January 2024, and Saudi FM Prince Faisal bin Farhan publicly welcomed this as part of a broader multipolar/hedging foreign policy. However, the description's core claim — that Saudi Arabia "accepted an invitation to join" — overstates what happened in 2023. Multiple contemporaneous sources (Al Jazeera, Al Arabiya) report the Saudi FM explicitly did NOT accept in 2023; he said the kingdom would "review the details" and take an "appropriate decision" before the Jan 1, 2024 date. Saudi Arabia in fact did not join at the start of 2024 as planned either, remained publicly non-committal/ambiguous through 2024 (Carnegie Endowment: "Why Is Saudi Arabia Hedging Its BRICS Invite?"), and only had its status resolved (with conflicting reports of full membership vs. continued non-decision, and later reports of a "suspended" membership) well after 2023. So: real event, correct country/year, but the described action (accepted/joined) is a material overstatement — the 2023 reality was "invited, non-committal," not "accepted."
